methods.name: initialize
methods.description: Initialize once before other requests. Unsupported u32 versions return -32002; repeated initialization returns -32009 after parameter validation.

methods.name: server.status
methods.description: Current live-worker count and history ownership; available during shutdown.

methods.name: server.stop
methods.description: Accept shutdown, clear the subscription and close after reply; acceptance does not mean cleanup has completed.

methods.name: sessions.list
methods.description: List retained sessions in daemon order. Includes host paths and process identity data; it conveys no runtime capabilities.

methods.name: sessions.get
methods.description: Read a session by immutable id or live agent name. Includes host paths and process identity data; it conveys no runtime capabilities.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.start
methods.description: Accept a host launch or recreate; retry keys return the original acceptance, not current readiness. For API-1 compatibility typed clients omit the empty host options map; nonempty maps remain present and are refused by host policy.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.stop
methods.description: Request teardown by immutable id or live agent name; acceptance does not mean cleanup finished.

methods.name: sessions.detach
methods.description: Detach the current terminal consumer, retaining the goblin.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.resize
methods.description: Resize by exact session id; dimensions are 1..1000 and a handler client must be attached.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.exec
methods.description: Run a host command with out-of-band stdio descriptors. The reply waits for exit or startup failure; closing this connection cancels its exec. Pin and existing validation/authority order are retained. See exec-descriptors, exec-lifecycle and exec-signal protocol rules.

methods.name: sessions.kill_execs
methods.description: Best-effort cancellation of every exec in the resolved sandbox. Dots in the session selector are replaced with slashes. Acceptance means KillAll was handed to the runtime, not completion.

methods.name: terminals.create
methods.description: Host create accepts ordered positional parameters session,argv,cwd,env,name,rows,cols,notify or a closed named object; only session is required. Sandbox create/list/close accept a closed named object or null-as-empty, never positional arrays, and may never supply session. The existing sandbox relay derives the session from the connection and preserves policy/refusal ordering. Host notify=true is rejected before command/name/size validation; sandbox notify may request an exit notice. Size defaults independently to 40 rows and 120 columns. Command/name/size, target/policy/init, capacity and uniqueness checks precede canonical init encoding and spawn transfer.

methods.name: terminals.list
methods.description: Terminal records expose id, nullable name, display label, host/agent origin, Unix-millisecond started_at, rows/cols and attached. IDs increase per session and are never reused; list orders started terminals oldest first, including host and agent origins. Creation answers only after Spawned; pending creates do not appear in lists. Listed records remain until the program ends. Snapshots retain their domain record bridge until C15. An exact retained session ID reads published terminal records even after stop (empty after terminal cleanup). Agent names resolve only while the runtime is live: a released name or unretained ID returns -32004, and a reused name selects the new live session.

methods.name: terminals.close
methods.description: Close requests cancellation of the terminal process group and returns accepted=true. The entry remains until exit. Sandbox callers can close only agent-created terminals; host-created ones return -32009. An explicit close suppresses exit notices; disconnect while creating does not cancel the already requested terminal. Existing lifecycle/notice ownership stays handwritten.

methods.name: terminals.read
methods.description: Read/send/wait first validate command-specific input, then resolve a live session/terminal; pending waits remain connection-owned, count toward the per-session limit of 16 and are withdrawn on disconnect. A connection serves no other call while waiting. Host detach ends only the frontend and keeps the program alive; the frontend stream remains reserved until it closes. Resize validates 1..500 rows/cols before target resolution and updates the existing screen/PTY through runtime commands. Sandbox attach/detach/resize remain unavailable and never enter its callable allowlist. Host read/send/wait accept named objects or positional arrays in their field order: session,terminal then source,lines for read; text,keys for send; match,regex,exit,timeout,lines for wait. Only session and terminal are required structurally. Sandbox calls omit session and retain object-only/null-as-empty rules. Send needs a string text (even empty) or nonempty keys; empty/null text and keys are distinguished. Wait selects one nonempty match string, Rust regex string, or exit=true; match/regex allow exit absent/null/false. Source, line/timeout/text/key bounds and regex compilation remain existing semantic validators in their original order. Request constraints separately describe cross-field requirements without changing generated record/default decoding. Read returns text,alternate_screen,rows,cols and optional truncated=true. Wait returns matched+line, timeout, or exited+nullable code/signal+text; truncated=true is present only when output is cut. Matching final output precedes exit reporting. Existing 256 KiB text and 4 KiB line limits remain. Legacy CLI readers independently normalize string text/status/line and signed 64-bit code/signal; missing/malformed/non-object values retain their old fallback, with unknown wait status reported as timeout. Send/detach/resize callers ignore successful result bodies. Current producers use generated precise DTOs; private runtime relays stay JSON until their owning migration.

methods.name: permissions.decide
methods.description: Approve or deny a pending request by immutable session, request and approval identities. All fields are required; named or ordered [session,request,approval,approved] forms are retained, unknown fields/null params are refused. String selectors are not prevalidated as identifiers: existing record lookup and identity/state checks determine absent versus stale errors. A located raid-owner request is refused before stale-identity checks; use raid methods instead. A dev shell approval requires its prepared preview identity; denial can cancel evaluation. Live requester/cancellation and runtime capacity checks retain their order. The result acknowledges the decision, not grant readiness, and echoes request/approved. No RPC parameter selects the deciding actor; the host endpoint supplies it.

errors.message: Stale decision, withdrawn requester or unfinished dev shell preview

x-notifications.name: exec.signal
x-notifications.connection-state: active exec only; ignored as no-id notification outside active exec
x-notifications.description: exec.signal is a host-client-to-daemon notification, with no id, only during an active exec. Named {signal:I32} or positional [I32] accepts SIGHUP=1, SIGINT=2, SIGTERM=15. Missing, invalid or unsupported signals, an unexpected method, or any id close the active-exec connection; cleanup cancels its exec only. Outside active exec, all no-id client notifications are ignored after envelope parsing; a host request with id and method exec.signal is unknown (-32601). It is never a callable method or sandbox capability.
